question: Should OpenClaw standardize these four core Gateway hosting profiles and the supporting public plugin readiness API, or keep deployment posture composition at the direct readiness-criteria/plugin layer?
rationale: This is a new deployment contract, configuration surface, readiness failure mode, and plugin SDK API spanning multiple unmerged PRs; correctness review cannot determine the desired permanent product boundary.

options.title: Approve staged core direction
options.body: Accept the readiness framework and core criteria first, then require this PR to rebase as a focused profile layer with package-installed Docker proof.

options.title: Keep composition operator-defined
options.body: Decline built-in profiles and retain direct `gateway.readiness` selection plus plugins for deployment-specific contracts.

options.title: Pause for RFC decision
options.body: Keep the branch open but defer implementation review until the linked RFC has an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Approve staged core direction
recommendation.body: Accept the readiness framework and core criteria first, then require this PR to rebase as a focused profile layer with package-installed Docker proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the linked implementation stack and can rescope or rebase the proposal after maintainers choose the product boundary.
